rounds.text: D.P. Abhushan Ltd is trading at an unjustifiably modest trailing P/E of 13.4x [E1], which sits at a steep discount to the broader consumer durables sector benchmark of 68.18x [E6]. This low valuation completely disconnects from the company's exceptional compounding ability, highlighted by a 5-year profit growth CAGR of 51% [E17] and a trailing twelve-month profit growth of 93% [E19]. Furthermore, return metrics remain elite, with a 3-year median ROE of 37% [E25] and an ROCE of 39.6% [E12], significantly outperforming the sector median ROCE of 9.9% [E73]. Management's aggressive top-line ambitions—targeting revenues of ₹4,800 crores in FY27 and ₹5,500 crores in FY28 [E74] alongside a long-term goal of 51 stores by 2030 [E76]—demonstrate clear operational momentum that is currently being ignored by the market. Conceded: operating cash flows turned negative at ₹-97 crores for March 2026 [E32] and borrowings rose to ₹290 crores [E36], yet the underlying business maintains stable store conversion rates of 82% to 83% [E87] and healthy same-store sales growth of approximately 20% [E88].

The bull claims that a trailing P/E of 13.4x [E1] and a P/E of 20.54x against a sector benchmark of 68.18x [E6] present a deep discount, but ignores that the company's price-to-book ratio of 6.03x trades at double the sector benchmark of 3.02x [E7]. Conceded: the company has demonstrated a 5-year profit CAGR of 51% [E17] and a trailing twelve-month profit growth of 93% [E19]. However, this reported earnings growth is completely detached from cash reality, as operating cash flow plunged to negative ₹97 crores and free cash flow dropped to negative ₹106 crores in March 2026 [E32, E33], resulting in a dismal cash conversion of -0.46x [E31]. Conceded: the 3-year median ROE is 37% [E25] and ROCE stands at 39.6% [E12]. Yet, borrowings jumped sharply to ₹290 crores in March 2026 from ₹184 crores a year earlier [E36], coinciding with negative institutional money flow and a deceleration in earnings growth [E41, E66]. Finally, while management cites aggressive revenue targets of ₹4,800 crores for FY27 and ₹5,500 crores for FY28 [E74], volatile and elevated gold prices have already impacted consumer affordability and muted volume growth [E92], forcing the company to put its proposed QIP on hold due to unfavorable market conditions [E89].

evidence.fact: Management aims to achieve 25% to 30% annual top-line growth by 2030.
evidence.quote: Over the next five years, by the end of 2030, we aim to grow at an annual rate of approximately 25% to 30%.

evidence.quote: Our long-term goal is to reach around 51 stores by 2030.

evidence.fact: Customer demand remained healthy across markets during the quarter, supported by consumption-led and investment-led purchases.

evidence.fact: Participation in gold exchange transactions strengthened further with old gold exchange contributing approximately 25% of total sales in Q1 FY27.
evidence.quote: Following recent government announcements and heightened customer awareness, participation in gold exchange transactions strengthened further, with old gold exchange contributing approximately 25% of total sales in Q1 FY27.

evidence.fact: Wedding jewellery accounts for ~60% of product mix, festival and lightweight jewellery ~25%, and gifting ~15%.
evidence.quote: From a product mix perspective, wedding jewellery continues to dominate at ~60%, followed by festival and lightweight jewellery at ~25%, and corporate and other gifting at ~15%, reflecting a well-diversified and demand-aligned portfolio.

evidence.fact: Locations have been finalized for upcoming showrooms in Jabalpur and Dahod with development progressing.
evidence.quote: The Company has successfully finalized locations for its upcoming showrooms in Jabalpur, Madhya Pradesh and Dahod, Gujarat, with all key agreements, approvals, and necessary formalities completed. Fit-out and showroom development activities are progressing at both locations, and the stores are expected to become operational shortly.

evidence.fact: The company expanded its retail footprint in Central India by inaugurating a new store in Dhar, taking total store count to 12.
evidence.quote: During the year, the Company further strengthened its footprint in Central India with the successful inauguration of a new s in Dhar, following the expansion in Ratlam earlier in the year, taking the total showroom network to 12.

evidence.fact: Management plans to open three to four COCO stores and add franchisee stores during the current financial year.
evidence.quote: For this financial year, we are planning to open around three to four COCO stores, along with adding more franchisees in a phased manner.

evidence.fact: Management expects gross margins to stay around 10% to 11%.
evidence.quote: As far as gross margins are concerned, we expect the business to maintain approximately 10% to 11%.

evidence.fact: FY26 EBITDA stood at INR 309.7 crores with margins improving by 234 basis points YoY to 7.61%.
evidence.quote: EBITDA stood at INR309.7 crores, reflecting a strong growth of 77% YoY, with EBITDA margins improving to 7.61%, an expansion of 234 basis points over FY25.

evidence.fact: The company expects finance costs to decrease gradually through GML, futures hedging, and leasing.
evidence.quote: And definitely, the finance cost is going to gradually go down also.

evidence.fact: Total retail store area reached ~53,650 sq. ft. supporting operations during FY26.
evidence.quote: Our total retail store area stood at ~53,650 sq. ft. supporting our growing scale of operations.

evidence.fact: Store conversion rates remained stable at ~82%–83% across locations.
evidence.quote: Our store-level conversion remains strong, with key stores such as Ratlam and Ratlam II delivering higher-than-average conversion levels, while overall conversion has remained largely stable at ~82%–83%.

evidence.fact: Same-store sales growth (SSG) reached approximately 20% YoY.
evidence.quote: So yeah, the number of the same-store sales growth is ~20% is the SSG growth.

evidence.fact: The company has put its proposed QIP on hold due to unfavourable market conditions.
evidence.quote: Yes, we are planning to undertake a QIP; however, we have currently put it on hold as market conditions are not favourable.

evidence.fact: Expansion plans for FY27 and FY28 will be funded via internal accruals.
evidence.quote: As far as our expansion plans for FY27 and FY28 are concerned, they will be executed through internal accruals as well.

evidence.fact: The company has no current plans for long-term borrowings.
evidence.quote: No, we have not yet planned for any long-term borrowings.

evidence.fact: Volatile and elevated gold prices in FY26 impacted consumer affordability and muted volume growth.
evidence.quote: Throughout FY26, gold prices were on an upward trajectory and quite volatile, which impacted affordability and consumer buying patterns. As a result, while value growth remained strong, volume growth was relatively muted.

evidence.fact: Recent statements by the Prime Minister created a slight short-term sentiment impact on demand.
evidence.quote: See, the Prime Minister’s statement may have a slight short-term impact on sentiment, but overall, we believe the underlying demand for gold remains strong.

evidence.fact: Management noted that elevated gold prices and broader industry challenges impacted demand volumes.
evidence.quote: Despite elevated gold prices and broader industry challenges impacting demand volumes, the Company demonstrated remarkable resilience, delivering steady revenue growth supported by robust customer footfalls, strong conversion rates, and deep-rooted brand trust.
